implementation: 10 WS APIs plus optional AttachTls, one native UTF-8 Text message per JSON-RPC document, optional binary input, bidirectional calls/notify/batch on existing Duplex/shared Server/Engine. Attach requires caller-validated HTTP Upgrade; no automatic HTTP handshake factory yet.

Bounded geometric receive assembly with old+new peak ledger, release above KeepReceiveBytes, read yield threshold and message admission deadline; original call-entry timeout includes encoding/admission; no replay after uncertain execution. Partial WS headers before MessageBegin require host TCP/TLS idle/read policy.

Actual immutable Duplex output reference credits through native SendRef: unmasked plain server avoids an adapter payload copy; masking and TLS copy in Core. No zero-copy or universal performance claim.

Close composes handler/job drain, gate entries, posts/timers, WS/native physical retirement and send release. Poll/Wait nudges cleanup on exhausted timers. Retained results survive Peer/Server/Engine destruction. No shared runtime or thread-per-peer.

Core normal EOF follows paused buffered messages, including final-byte Data and pending MessageEnd. Native TLS can close reentrantly inside Consume; retain the existing TLS owner until Resume finishes, or explicit Worker Close/cross-thread Abort abandons it. Errors do not wait for abandoned readers. No added TLS alias, receive queue, timer or thread.

Parent a725e505 fails the same public EOF harness on both hosts as an expected negative control, excluded from primary counts.
failure_scope: Retain failed compile/runtime/tooling attempts and expected negative controls. Corrections include unsigned diagnostic atomics/public attach prefix, malformed-frame bytewise sends after early rejection, first native error versus close timeout, TCP EOF/Resume race and TLS reentrant final-byte close, required docs prefixes and explicit extension size config. Initial owned EOF prototype used a borrowed TLS bootstrap and was rejected; final probe uses owned TLS/WS contexts and checks exact four-to-one context credits. A prior TSan program passed but its script final guard caught concurrent edits to two unused diagnostics; final cohort TSan passes fully. User pause and later superseded old-code validation were explicitly interrupted, never counted as successful completion.
